“I am thinking that very few, if any, of the SpaceX Falcon 9 first stages are going to be re-used for more than 3 or so flights,” Cantrell said.

Only initially. It's still a developing thing so there is still lots of data to gather about what parts can be reused and how much.

For example, this last launch from Vandenberg, used new, larger titanium cast grid fins. They learned rather quickly that the original aluminum ones don't hold up to well to certain kinds of reentry and can't really be used more than once. The new titanium ones came back still looking brand new.

The Falcon 9s currently being launched and reflown aren't even the final version. They are block 3. Block 4 is coming soon and they should be making block 5 by the end of the year. Block 5 is slated to be the final version and those will end up being reused the most.
